source: Malik (1990) JCP 86:376 Fig. 4: M=10, R=2000, cooled wall T_w/T_adb=0.1, alpha=0.105 second-mode eigenfunctions (refPapers/NewPapers/figures/malik1990_fig4_eigenfunctions_M10.png).
quantity: second-mode temperature eigenFUNCTION (T_hat_r, T_hat_i vs y)
verdict_reason: Eigenvector (mode-structure) validation. The overlay plots pyMack's temperature eigenfunction CURVES over Malik's own DIGITISED Fig.4 points (single Temperature panel, profile orientation, y vertical). BOTH the real and imaginary temperature eigenfunctions AGREE with Malik under one shared complex T_hat scaling (global phase fixed so T_hat_r is real and +1 at its peak -- Malik's convention; T_hat_i is NOT renormalised separately). pyMack's T_hat_r lies on Malik's digitised T_hat_r (RMS = 0.052 over 0<y<20): shallow near-wall negative lobe (~-0.5), zero-crossing near y~6, LOWER of the two rising curves in y~6-11, and the +1 peak at y~13.3 (Malik y~13, a 2.3% location match). pyMack's T_hat_i lies on Malik's digitised T_hat_i (RMS = 0.082): deeper near-wall dip (~-0.6), UPPER of the two rising curves in y~6-11, the rounded +0.45 hump at y~11, and the steep descent to the -0.55 dip at y~15.5 (the 'T_l' curve). The temperature fluctuation dominates ( |T_hat|/|u_hat| = 14.4 ), the hallmark of the hypersonic Mack mode. Velocity and pressure eigenfunctions are omitted (too hard to digitise reliably: overlapping near-axis curves). This opens the eigenvector-validation axis (all other anchors check eigenvalues only). Mirror of validation/test_malik_fig4_eigenfunction.py.
pymack_provenance: pymack.solver.solve_temporal_compressible eigenvector (same case as malik_case4), block [u,v,T,p], normalized to unit peak |T|; N=200, y_max=75, length_scale='L_star'.
